To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the gut microbiome can be classified into three different communities, (2) the structure of the microbiome is associated to the occurrence of postoperative complications and (3) patients with a microbiome resembling community B are more likely to experience postoperative complications.

the gut microbiome of patients with postoperative complications is dominated by Akkermansiae, Enterobacteriales and Bacteroidaceae, and is characterized by a lower abundance of Prevotellaceae, Lachnospira and Bacteroidetes.
